issues.legal_issue: A claimant seeking to invalidate a parent's property alienations on the ground that the parent was a minor must prove the parent's minority at the time of the alienations.
material_facts: The claimant bore the burden of proving that the parent was a minor when the sale deeds were executed.

A school certificate stating the parent's birth date was proved only by a clerk who identified the handwriting; the issuer was not examined, the original admission register was not proved, and the clerk could not identify who made the original entry.
Evidence that the parent had attended another school was not denied, but records from that school were not produced; family horoscopes were also withheld.
The parent had contested an earlier suit without pleading minority, managed property, and was described as a major in registered documents and court records before executing the challenged deeds.
issues.conclusion: The evidence supported the finding that the parent was not a minor when the deeds were executed, so the minority-based challenge failed.
issues.legal_principle: The burden of proving alleged minority rested on the claimant. A certificate whose contents were not proved by a competent witness or by the underlying record could not establish the stated birth date; the court assessed it against the other evidence, including the parent's conduct and records describing the parent as an adult. The judgment cites no statutory provision or earlier case for this issue.

rule.if: suit_challenges_parental_alienations and claimant_bears_burden_of_proving_minority and certificate_contents_not_proved and independent_evidence_supports_adulthood and age_records_withheld

predicates.suit_challenges_parental_alienations: A claimant brings a suit to challenge property alienations made by a parent.
predicates.claimant_bears_burden_of_proving_minorit: The claimant is responsible for proving that the parent was a minor when the alienations were made.
predicates.certificate_contents_not_proved: A certificate offered to establish the parent's age is not supported by competent proof of its contents or its underlying record.
predicates.independent_evidence_supports_adulthood: Other evidence, such as the parent's conduct or contemporaneous records, supports that the parent was an adult at the relevant time.
predicates.age_records_withheld: The claimant does not produce relevant age or family records that could bear on the parent's age.

issues.definition: When a claimant challenging a parent's alienations bears the burden of proving minority, an unproved certificate, contrary evidence of adulthood, and withheld age records lead to the minority-based challenge failing.

issues.legal_issue: A parent's property alienations made for antecedent debts or legal necessity are not invalidated by a descendant's challenge alleging lack of consideration or necessity.
material_facts: The first sale deed was found to have been executed to discharge earlier debts, including mortgage dues, a debt arising from a decree, and other amounts owed to creditors.
The second sale deed was found to have funded earlier decretal and rent dues, arrears of rent, a creditor's claim, payments to other creditors, and domestic needs.
The court upheld the findings that the deeds were supported by consideration and that the second deed was also supported by legal necessity.
issues.conclusion: The findings that the sales discharged antecedent debts and that the second sale was supported by legal necessity were correct; the challenge to the deeds on these grounds failed.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied the principle that an alienation by a parent for payment of antecedent debts may bind the descendant, and upheld the alienation also found to be for legal necessity. It relied on the evidence tracing the sale consideration to debts and necessary payments. The judgment cites no statutory provision or earlier case for this issue.

predicates.suit_challenges_parental_alienations: A descendant brings a suit to challenge property alienations made by a parent.
predicates.sale_consideration_applied_to_antecedent: The evidence shows that the sale consideration was applied to the parent's earlier debts or to payments needed for the family or property.

issues.definition: When a descendant challenges a parent's alienations and the consideration was applied to antecedent debts or legal necessity, the alienations bind the descendant and the consideration challenge fails.

issues.legal_issue: An allegation that a parent who made a property alienation led an immoral life does not, by itself, invalidate the alienation.
material_facts: The claimant and the parent both testified that the parent had led an immoral life.
The claimant relied on that allegation in challenging the sale deeds.
issues.conclusion: The allegation of the parent's immoral life did not nullify the sale deeds.
issues.legal_principle: The court held that the parent's alleged immoral life did not, on its own, nullify the documents. The judgment cites no statutory provision or earlier case for this issue.

predicates.suit_challenges_parental_alienation: A claimant brings a suit to challenge a property alienation made by a parent.
predicates.vendor_immoral_life_alleged: The claimant alleges that the parent who made the alienation led an immoral life.

issues.definition: When a claimant challenges a parent's alienation and alleges that the parent led an immoral life, that allegation alone does not invalidate the alienation.
